YOUR FIRST ENGLISH BOOK

Welcome, Little Learner!

Let's learn the English alphabet together!

There are 26 letters. Every letter has a capital letter and a small letter.

Look at each model, say the letter, copy it, and write it by yourself.

Use the word example to practice your new letter.

LEARN IN FOUR STEPSTry this on every page.
1LookLook at the black model.
2SaySay the letter aloud.
3CopyFollow the guide lines.
4WriteWrite it by yourself.

In this book, you will:

Write big and small letters, practice one word for every letter, and speak with a new friend.

Get ready:

Find a pencil, sit comfortably, and take your time. Good writing grows with practice.

26English letters
4guide lines
2conversations
You can do it! One letter at a time.

FOUR GUIDE LINES

How to Use the Four Guide Lines

The four lines help you write each letter in the right place.

TOP LINE
MIDDLE LINE
BASE LINE
BOTTOM LINE
SEE HOW LETTERS SITBlack models inside the four guide lines.
CAPITAL LETTERSTOP TO BASE
A A A AMODEL
SMALL LETTERSMIDDLE TO BASE
a a a aMODEL
LETTER TAILSBASE TO BOTTOM
p p p pMODEL
1. Most capital letters start at the top line and sit on the base line.
2. Small letters usually sit between the middle line and the base line.
3. Tall small letters reach the top line. Letter tails go down to the bottom line.
4. Capital J and Q can dip below the base line.
Remember: Keep each letter in its place. Look at the model before you write.

MY INTRODUCTION
SPEAKING ABOUT YOU

This Is Me!

Use the words to tell a new friend about yourself.

Hello! My name is _______________.
I am ______ years old.
I like _________________________.
My favorite color is ____________.
Nice to meet you!
Write your name on the four guide lines.
Write one thing you like on the four guide lines.
Look up, smile, and say hello!
